title: First law of thermodynamics and p–V work; Thermodynamic processes and heat engines
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: T07-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; T07-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; T08-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; T07-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: T07-1#N.3c, T08-1#N.3b, T07-1#N.9, T08-1#N.11, T07-1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Heating
items.clue: Energy crossing a boundary because of a temperature difference.

items.label: Work
items.clue: Energy crossing a boundary because a force moves it, as with a piston.

items.label: Isothermal process
items.clue: Change at constant temperature, following PV = constant; ΔU = 0 for an ideal gas.

items.label: Internal energy
items.clue: Symbol U: random kinetic plus potential contributions of the particles; a property of the state.

questions.stem: A gas in a cylinder is compressed by a piston. During the compression, 250 J of work is done on the gas, and 400 J of energy is transferred from the gas to its surroundings by cooling. What is the change in the internal energy of the gas?

An ideal gas in a cylinder is compressed slowly, so that its temperature stays constant. The work done on the gas during the compression is W, which is positive. Which statement about the energy transferred by heating or cooling is correct?

options.text: Energy equal to W is transferred into the gas by heating.
No energy is transferred, since the temperature stays fixed.
Less than W leaves by cooling; the rest is stored in the gas.
Energy equal to W is transferred out of the gas by cooling.

questions.stem: A sample of 8.0 g of helium, a monatomic ideal gas of molar mass 4.0 g mol⁻¹, is heated at constant pressure from 20 °C to 80 °C. The thermal energy supplied is 2.49 × 10³ J. R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the change in internal energy ΔU of the helium?

Two identical samples of ideal gas start in the same state. Each is compressed to half its volume: one slowly, in good thermal contact with a water bath (isothermal); the other quickly, in an insulated cylinder (adiabatic). Which statement is correct?

options.text: The isothermal compression needs more work, because its gas stays at the higher temperature.
The adiabatic compression needs more work and ends at the higher pressure.
Both need the same work, because they start in the same state and end at the same volume.
The adiabatic compression needs more work, but both end at the same pressure, as the volumes match.

questions.stem: An ideal gas is in a cylinder whose walls and piston are perfectly insulated. The gas expands, pushing the piston outwards. What happens to the temperature of the gas?

options.text: It stays the same, because no energy is transferred to or from the gas by heating.
It falls, because the gas does work on the piston and no energy enters by heating.
It rises, because the molecules move further apart and gain energy as they spread out.
It stays the same, because the fall in pressure exactly balances the rise in volume.
